taxonomyNote: NatureServe notes it was regarded as conspecific with African P. lucidus by AOU (1983, 1998) and forms a superspecies with P. capillatus.
fieldMarks: Large and bulky, 84-100 cm, with a relatively short tail, big head and thick bill
Adult has a broad white band across the throat behind bare yellow face skin; breeding birds show white flank patches
Immature brownish, resembling Double-crested Cormorant but usually with brown neck and chest contrasting with a white belly
Throat pouch dull yellow, not orange
behavior: Migrates in flocks, paralleling the coastline a short distance offshore
Most foraging within 10 ft of the surface, diving to about 30 ft; feeds almost entirely on fish
Nests on rocky cliffs of coasts and islands; wintering birds often around rock jetties and recently on large inland rivers
habitat: Mainly coastal, over shallow waters close to shore, especially sheltered bays; nests on sea cliffs. In the Old World regularly far inland on lakes, rivers and swamps.
range: In North America breeds along the Atlantic coast from the Gulf of St. Lawrence and southwestern Newfoundland to Nova Scotia (recolonized Maine); winters from the breeding range south to North Carolina, sometimes farther. Also Iceland, southwestern Greenland and much of the Old World.

lookalikes.name: Double-crested cormorant
lookalikes.howToTell: Smaller; orange throat pouch and no broad white throat band or white flank patches.
